housing.summary: Turku's rental market is smaller and cheaper than Helsinki. Most rentals are found through online portals and require a Finnish personal identity code (henkilotunnus) and often proof of income or employment. Furnished units are less common; deposits are typically 1-2 months' rent. Student housing (TYS) is widely available given the large university population.

banking.summary: Opening a Finnish bank account generally requires a passport/ID, a residence permit or proof of legal residence, a Finnish personal identity code (henkilotunnus), and often proof of address or employment. Strong customer authentication and online banking credentials (verkkopankkitunnukset) are central to daily life in Finland. Major banks operate branches in Turku.
required_docs: Residence permit / proof of legal residence

schools.summary: Turku offers public Finnish- and Swedish-language schooling (Turku is officially bilingual) plus international options. Turku International School provides English-language instruction, and IB programmes are available in the region. Public basic education is free.

legal_admin.summary: New residents register their move and obtain a Finnish personal identity code (henkilotunnus) through the Digital and Population Data Services Agency (DVV). EU/EEA citizens register their right of residence; non-EU nationals need a residence permit from Migri before registering. Local registration establishes access to municipal services.
legal_admin.registration_step: Register residence and obtain a personal identity code (henkilotunnus) at the Digital and Population Data Services Agency (DVV)

tax_finance.summary: Employees must obtain a tax card (verokortti) from the Finnish Tax Administration (Vero) so the correct withholding rate is applied to salary. Newly arrived foreign workers may need to visit a tax office in person. Taxation is administered nationally, so the process in Turku is the same as elsewhere in Finland.
tax_finance.tax_id_name: Henkilotunnus (Finnish personal identity code) with verokortti (tax card)

transport.summary: Turku's regional public transport is operated under the Foli brand, covering buses across Turku and neighbouring municipalities, plus the Fori city ferry across the Aura river. Tickets use a rechargeable travel card or mobile app. Monthly season tickets are available at resident rates. Non-EU/EEA driving licences generally must be exchanged within a limited period after establishing residence.
transport.driving_licence_exchange: EU/EEA licences are valid; many non-EU/EEA licences must be exchanged for a Finnish licence within a set period after establishing residence (conditions depend on country of origin)
transport.healthcare_registration: Access to public healthcare follows municipal registration and Kela (social insurance) coverage; register with local health services after obtaining a personal identity code
